Question B-003-013-007.

Why the correct answer is right: Stronger audio causes a wider frequency swing in FM, so the carrier deviation becomes larger.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "By a larger deviation of the carrier frequency": This is the correct choice because stronger audio causes a wider frequency swing in FM, so the carrier deviation becomes larger.
- sourceIndex 1: "By a larger amplitude of the carrier": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from By a larger deviation of the carrier frequency. In FM deviation, FM receiver behaviour, and local VHF/UHF voice practice, carrier terminology is being applied to the wrong modulation condition here.
- sourceIndex 2: "By a larger pulse width in the transmitted wave train": This answer would fit a different fault than By a larger deviation of the carrier frequency. In FM deviation, FM receiver behaviour, and local VHF/UHF voice practice, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 3: "By a larger peak envelope power": This option confuses another station topic with By a larger deviation of the carrier frequency. In FM deviation, FM receiver behaviour, and local VHF/UHF voice practice, power alone is not the control or safety mechanism being tested in this item.
